family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Broad family: check for latex, simple usually opposite/whorled leaves and a fused 5-lobed corolla. In local milkweeds/milkvines, go straight to the corona, gynostegium and pollinarium.
family_diagnostics.broad_family: Five stamens are associated closely with the fused corolla/stylar head; the superior gynoecium is built from two carpels.
family_diagnostics.milkweed_specialization: In Asclepiadoideae, stamens and stylar head form a gynostegium and pollen is packaged into pollinia/pollinaria.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Often one or two follicles with comose seeds on the milkweed side, but broad Apocynaceae fruit is more diverse.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Treat corona + gynostegium + pollinia as a powerful derived milkweed signature, not as a requirement for every Apocynaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → exception/tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Learn the broad dogbane plan first, then zoom into the bizarre specialized milkweed machinery.

steps.title: 1 · Broad family doorway
steps.look_for: Simple entire leaves plus latex and a fused flower; these are broad-family clues, not final proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the learner from defining the whole family only by milkweed structures.

steps.title: 2 · Find the corona
steps.look_for: Five hoods surrounding the central gynostegium; horns may project from the hoods depending on species.
steps.why_it_matters: The corona is one of the fastest Asclepias-level structures to learn.

steps.title: 3 · Find the gynostegium
steps.look_for: The fused reproductive column in the center rather than separate ordinary stamens and stigma.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the structural heart of the milkweed pollination mechanism.

steps.title: 4 · Follow flower to follicle
steps.look_for: A developing or mature follicle derived from one of the two carpels; the partner often aborts.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit architecture links the odd flower back to the two-carpel family plan.

steps.title: 5 · Compare a milkvine
steps.look_for: Twining habit, opposite cordate leaves and a specialized gynostegium/corona flower unlike a morning-glory.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that the milkweed mechanism is not limited to upright Asclepias.

comparisons.title: Apocynaceae vs Convolvulaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have fused corollas and vines. Milkweed-side Apocynaceae has gynostegium/corona/pollinarium machinery and follicle fruit; morning-glories do not.

comparisons.title: Broad family vs milkweed group
comparisons.rule: Corona, gynostegium and pollinia are derived milkweed-side traits. Broad Apocynaceae is more diverse.

visual_lesson.caveat: The current local project is intentionally strongest on Asclepiadoideae; one non-Asclepiadoideae breadth card remains future visual polish.
